title: Benchmarking Coding Agents on New vs Legacy Codebases — Denys Linkov, Wisedocs
talk_summary: Speaker describes a 6-month refactor of 10 legacy repos into a monorepo and benchmarks coding agents on replicating/refactoring tasks. He finds newer models/harnesses need less manual intervention but still fail zero-shot, and recommends high-accuracy task-duration thresholds, specs/plans, local review checks, and sandbox-friendly repo structure.

takeaways.what_they_do: They judge agent autonomy by high-accuracy success rates over task duration, not 50% pass rates, because long runs with coin-flip reliability waste compute and attention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I actually think it's much better to measure the accuracy at 90% or 99% because this is where the mental model is most efficient.
takeaways.numbers: Success declines significantly at the 4-hour mark; some tasks fail even before 15 minutes.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat incomplete prompts, plans, or requirements as a main cause of failed agent runs, and require a constructed plan/spec before handing work off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Who here has kicked off an agent and realized that either the prompt, the plan, or the requirements were incomplete or missing?

takeaways.technique: Local review skills before PR review
takeaways.what_they_do: They run local review skills/checks on code before formal PR review, so obvious issues are caught cheaply before human or heavier review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We did some local checks where we ran skills to say, 'Hey, review this code. Make sure that it's good.'

takeaways.what_they_do: They moved multiple repos into a monorepo because end-to-end testing, verification, deployment, and sandbox setup are harder across many repos.
takeaways.numbers: 10 repos consolidated into a monorepo; refactor took about 6 months.

takeaways.what_they_do: They found a zero-shot agent appeared to finish but only wrote scaffolding, so they inspected for missing real components and deployment/bootstrap steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it actually just implemented a bunch of scaffolding and didn't implement the models
takeaways.numbers: GPT 5.5 extra high wrote 2,000 lines in 10m22s but only scaffolding.

takeaways.what_they_do: They observed newer harnesses use sub-agents, plan calls, shell commands, and verification, which costs more in execution but reduces manual intervention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we get sub-agents, we get some of those plan calls, we get different shell commands, and we get different verifications.
takeaways.numbers: O3 took 3 hours with 10 major mistakes; Sonnet 4.6 needed one extra iteration; Opus one-shot it; overall ~1/5 the time.
